real_s1.explanation: The unit responds to dogs and dog-like animals such as wolves and lesser pandas, and is weakest when the animal faces or points to the left. The clearest and most specific effect is right-facing over left-facing (rows 1 and 2). It held on new photos while similar units did not show it. Toward- or away-from-camera views also beat left-facing strongly on new photos, though similar units share part of that. Its preference for centered subjects over right-third subjects held, but similar units share it, so it is not particular to this unit. Preferences for large subjects and against cool tints were not tested and are partly shared.

Right-facing animals drive it more strongly, and this held on new photos while the similar units did not show it. Animals facing toward or away from the camera also beat left-facing ones, but the similar units largely share that contrast. The unit also prefers warm color casts over cool ones, which held on new photos, and leans toward large, centered, frame-filling subjects, a preference partly shared with similar units. The 'no clear facing direction' versus left contrast did not hold on new photos.

real_s3.explanation: The unit responds to dogs and other furry canid-like animals (fluffy dogs, wolves, lesser panda). What is particular to it is a left-facing penalty: it is much weaker when the animal faces or points left than when it faces right or toward the camera. It also prefers warm color casts over cool ones and large, centered subjects. The color and size preferences are partly shared with similar units. The left-facing penalty, and the right-versus-left contrast especially, is distinctive to this unit.
